subject: Renewal packaging: staged uplift, co-term options, and interim SLA credit
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-inc.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: Renewal packaging and uplift — initial ask

Hi Mateo,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting renewal planning for Acme and want to understand options for (a) handling a mid-contract growth spike we expect in Q1, (b) co-terming our various SKUs into a single annual contract, and (c) any temporary SLA or credit you can offer during the ramp.

Can you share a few alternative structures — e.g., staged uplift, one-time top-up, or a voucher approach — and what the pricing/discount tradeoffs look like? Procurement is asking for an executable path by Nov 30 so we can include it in our renewal packet. I attached our current usage snapshot — happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Therapeutics
attachments: Acme_Renewal_Summary_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-inc.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal packaging and uplift — initial ask

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and the summary. Quick reply with three pragmatic paths and what we’d need for each: 

1) Staged top-up (recommended for predictable ramp)
   - Add a temporary top-up bucket for the next 3 months (consumption pre-purchased).
   - Apply a one-time 8% uplift discount off list for the first billing period if committed to a 12-month co-term at signature.
   - Requires PO and standard amendment; minimal legal work.

2) Voucher / credit pool (flexible, lower up-front commitment)
   - Pre-purchased voucher that draws down against usage; refund window limited.
   - 5% pricing uplift vs. staged top-up, but no long-term commit required.

3) Seat-to-consumption exchange + annualize (best for teams shifting usage patterns)
   - Convert X seats to a consumption baseline and annualize at a blended rate.
   - We can offer a stepped discount: 6% year-1 blended if you consolidate to a single co-term and increase commit by >=15%.

On the SLA credit: we can offer an interim goodwill credit (one-time invoice credit) tied to the first month of ramp for visibility while we scale capacity. I’ll loop in finance/legal to confirm level-of-credit and signoff.

I attached a pricing worksheet with ballpark numbers for each path (redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx). Can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through which path fits you best?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx)
From: contracts@acme-inc.com
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal packaging and uplift — procurement note

Mateo — thanks. A couple of procurement items: 
- Any concession needs to be reflected as a term in the amendment (not off-invoice).
- We need a maximum liability cap for the ramp bucket and dates for when the top-up expires.
- The SLA credit is acceptable if it is a documented invoice credit with an explicit trigger (e.g., >1 hour outage impacting requests).

If you can provide a short amendment draft and the exact credit formula, we’ll accelerate signoff.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Acme Therapeutics
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:18:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Acme renewal — recommended concession and legal checklist

Marissa / Olga / Kim — internal summary and ask. Sanjay’s procurement wants a documented amendment and explicit SLA credit formula. My recommended path to close quickly:

- Offer: Staged top-up (3 months) + one-time SLA invoice credit (applied within first invoice after ramp) + consolidate to 12-month co-term on signature.
- Commercial concession: 10% off the top-up invoice for month 1 (to show commitment), then revert to standard blended rates thereafter. If they consolidate commit by signature (>=12 months co-term, +15% baseline uplift), provide a 6% blended discount on the annualized baseline.
- Legal asks: amendment wording for top-up bucket size, expiry date (90 days), liability cap on the top-up to the pre-approved bucket, SLA credit trigger and calculation, and DocuSign flow.

Risks / notes:
- Margin: 10% initial concession on a large top-up could be material; propose limiting concession to the top-up bucket only (not baseline).
- Pre-approve up to $45k of invoice credits for the account owner (Marissa) to sign off without legal for speed; anything higher -> legal review.

Olga — can you draft a short amendment skeleton with the SLA credit formula and the liability cap language? Marissa — can you pre-approve the $45k credit max for this account for rapid closure? Kim — please plan a 30-min sync with Sanjay to walk numbers.

Thanks,
Mateo
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-inc.com>, contracts@acme-inc.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal packaging and uplift — agreed path and next steps

Sanjay — appreciate the quick turn. We’ve agreed the following path: 

1) Staged top-up: one-time pre-purchase bucket sized at your requested Q1 ramp estimate, expires 90 days after purchase. We’ll add this as Amendment A to your Master Subscription Agreement.

2) Commercials: 10% credit applied to the top-up invoice for month 1 (on-invoice credit), then standard blended consumption pricing from month 2 onward. If you commit to co-term and a baseline uplift >=15% at signature, we’ll apply a 6% blended discount to the annualized baseline.

3) SLA credit: one-time invoice credit triggered by a verified outage (defined in Amendment A). Cap for early invoice credits pre-approved up to $45,000; anything above requires legal approval.

4) Next steps: Olga is drafting the amendment and will post a DocuSign envelope (link below). Please review and aim for signature by Nov 30 to meet your procurement timeline. I attached the updated pricing worksheet and included the DocuSign link for convenience.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embedded-sign/abc123
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-RNWL-7
Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx

If that all looks good, I’ll send the amendment draft and schedule a 30-minute call to walk legal language.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
